core.title: Start journeys from the reference strategy; justify alternatives
core.given: A plan defines or revises a journey's execution strategy; strategies are candidate ways to meet declared behavioral obligations.
core.when: The planner selects, changes or combines strategies.
core.then: Begin with the reference strategy, then consider alternatives or combinations only when latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism or complexity requirements, or measured workloads, justify their complexity.
prefer: Treat strategies as orthogonal, combinable candidates; none is universally best. The baseline is the reference strategy convention of this convention set.
Keep ownership: flow routers select guarded alternatives, journeys compose control flow, user/system flows stay linear, product capabilities optimize internals.
Plan only behavior the plan and runtime actually support; preserve contracts, artifacts, prerequisites, side effects, error paths and terminal outcomes.
Prove equivalence with behavioral tests; back performance claims with reproducible benchmarks.
avoid: Exploring alternatives without a requirement or measured workload that justifies the complexity.
Using a strategy choice to bypass flow routers, user/system flows, continuations or acceptances.
Assuming fork/join, stream or speculation exists; missing capability needs separate implementation and accepted proof.
Slipping observable behavior changes in via a strategy; they need their own accepted route.
core.why: Alternatives add complexity and risk to behavior that must stay equivalent. This is advisory planner guidance owned by this stack's convention set, not a new runtime mode or an independently enforced rule; existing journey, flow router and acceptance validators stay authoritative.
evidence: Reviewer can establish that the journey began from the reference strategy and that any alternative or combination considered is justified by a latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism or complexity requirement or by a measured workload.
Behavioral tests show the alternative preserves contracts, artifacts, prerequisites, side effects, error paths and terminal outcomes.
Performance claims are backed by reproducible benchmarks.
Every used capability (fork/join, stream, speculation) is supported by the plan and runtime or has a separate implementation with accepted proof.
Existing journey, flow router and acceptance validators still pass; they remain authoritative.
verification: Advisory disposition at severity 3: not independently enforced and not a new runtime mode; report as guidance and defer to the existing journey, flow router and acceptance validators, which remain authoritative.
A justification is checked against the requirement axes latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism and complexity; a measured workload is also an accepted justification.

Activation observability: the task-term fact is a discovery signal, not a standalone firing condition; the phase fact needs an observer that knows the agent is authoring a plan artifact or acceptance rather than implementing; the change fact needs a diff-level observer over journey plan artifacts; the rule fires on every journey strategy selection or revision.

The finding fact (non-reference strategy considered or chosen without justification) is llm_judged and diagnostic only: it reports non-compliance after the rule has fired and is never an activation prerequisite.

values: journey execution strategy selected, changed or combined (any strategy to any other)
non-reference strategy considered or chosen without requirement or measured-workload justification

fires: Planner authors a new journey and selects how its steps execute (reference or any alternative/combination).
Planner revises an existing journey's strategy in any direction: reference to alternative, alternative to another alternative, alternative back to reference, or adding a combined strategy.
Strategy change is motivated by latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism or complexity concerns.
Plan proposes fork/join, streaming or speculation that the runtime may not yet support.
doesNotFire: A product capability optimizes its own internals without changing journey control flow.
Edits to a journey that do not touch its execution strategy (e.g. renaming, doc wording).
Coder implementing an already-accepted plan with no strategy decision to make.

bunOnly.text: The baseline is the reference strategy convention (planner.journey.strategy.reference).
bunOnly.reason: Names the concrete sibling-convention id in the ATDD-Bun catalog; each stack's realization points at its own reference-strategy convention id, so the core refers to it generically and the id is restored on instantiation.

bunOnly.text: This is Bun-owned advisory planner guidance
bunOnly.reason: Attributes ownership of the guidance to the Bun stack; the neutral core attributes it to the owning stack's convention set without naming a stack.

neutralityNotes: This rule is pure plan-model planner guidance: it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. Journey, user/system flow, product capability, acceptance, desired-outcome-level plan artifacts and the planner/coder workflow roles are ATDD methodology vocabulary shared across stacks (the vocabulary's urn group already carries journey, user/system flow, product capability, desired outcome and acceptance), so they stay in the core; 'flow router' and 'continuation' have no vocabulary key, but the core needs only their names as plan-model guard rails, not their shapes, so no key is proposed. 'fork/join', 'stream' and 'speculation' are generic concurrency capabilities, and 'runtime' is the generic execution runtime. The only stack-specific strings are the concrete sibling-convention id in prefer[0] and the 'Bun-owned' attribution in why; both are carried in bunOnly so instantiation restores the exact Bun text. The activation fact notes cannot be expressed in the core fact schema (fact/values/observability only); their semantics — discovery-only task terms, the new observers needed for phase and change, the diagnostic-only finding that is never an activation prerequisite, and firing on every strategy selection or revision — are preserved in core.verification. fires and doesNotFire entries are not separately numbered items and are carried verbatim in the core activation.
